item.title: Could voting break the plastics treaty deadlock?
item.description: Disputes over voting rules have allowed a small group of countries to block ambition – stalling a global treaty to curb plastic production and pollution.

item.title: Trump, China and 300 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil
item.description: As the US powers ahead with its plans to recover Latin America’s ‘oil El Dorado’, we explore Venezuela’s environmental and geopolitical outlook.

item.title: How ‘mid-level bureaucrats’ are helping to shape Chinese climate policy
item.description: Local officials are often viewed as relatively weak actors in China’s governance structure, largely implementing policies issued from the central level.

item.title: A global race for rare earth minerals underpins the green transition
item.description: The shift to a green economy has deepened global dependence on rare earth elements, prompting countries to pursue collaboration while simultaneously racing to secure local resources.

item.title: Skills gap, high cost and poor data slowing climate reporting by Singapore listed firms
item.description: But the majority SGX-listed firms polled have begun adopting the ISSB standards already, which they say can attract investors and improve corporate reputation, an industry study finds.

item.title: How local energy networks are saving lives across the world
item.description: In the US and the Global South, local ‘microgrid’ power networks are being adopted in neighbourhoods battling rising heat.

item.title: The inequalities that Delhi’s smog hides
item.description: Beyond costly air purifiers lies a city trapped by air pollution, with dense neighbourhoods and traditional gender roles exacerbating health impacts for the lower income.

item.title: Philanthropy must dive deeper to save the ocean
item.description: Philanthropy's impact depends less on the amounts raised and more on how effectively it connects people and organisations working to build a sustainable blue economy.

item.title: Experts: Will Chinese wind power help or hinder Europe’s climate goals?
item.description: The European Union and the UK are not on track to meet their 2030 offshore wind targets.

item.title: Kerala Adivasi families emancipated by growing yam, tapioca
item.description: From depending on others for food to cultivating a sustainable and marketable crop, marginalised tribes in Kerala are reclaiming their livelihoods one tuber at a time.
